sections.heading: What are comparatives and superlatives?
paragraphs: In Hungarian, comparison is formed by modifying the adjective. Just like in English, you can compare two things (comparative) or say something is the most (superlative).

sections.heading: Comparative and superlative in Hungarian
paragraphs: The comparative is formed by adding -bb to the adjective.
To form the superlative, use the prefix a leg- + the comparative form.

rows: Ő magasabb, mint én. – He is taller than me.
Ő a legmagasabb a csoportban. – He is the tallest in the group.
A víz hideg. – The water is cold.
Ma hidegebb van, mint tegnap. – Today is colder than yesterday.
Ez a leghidegebb nap. – This is the coldest day.

sections.heading: Important points
list: The basic rule: adjective + bb → comparative.
Use mint (than) to compare two things: nagyobb, mint...
For superlatives, use the article a (or az) and the prefix leg-.
Some adjectives change slightly before adding -bb (e.g., szép → szebb).

sections.heading: Examples
list: Ez a ház nagyobb, mint a másik. – This house is bigger than the other.
Ő a legokosabb diák. – He/She is the smartest student.
A leves melegebb, mint a tea. – The soup is warmer than the tea.
Ez a legjobb film. – This is the best movie.
